spec_issues: Title and constraint do not match. The id says 'make-the-mambatm-turbulence-restorer-safe-on-mild-turbulence-without-los[ing]...', the overview says 'reward of 0 if its PSNR averaged over strengths 6, 8 and 10 falls over 0.1 decibels below the starter's', and the prompt says 'at most a 0.1 dB drop from baseline quality on the strongest turbulence'. The public verifier implements the overview: STRONG_BINS=(6,8,10), STRONG_MARGIN_DB=0.1, valid=int(strong_gate_passed) (run_sweep.py, gpt-6-astra__6RCWGpu [3]). The prompt's 'strongest turbulence' is vague but consistent.

The gate never binds. Every trial improves strong-bin PSNR on the public sweep by +0.80 dB (Gemini Flash Taw69S6) to +1.97 dB (Fable eTezLSD), because fine-tuning on the full simulator range helps strong turbulence too. The task therefore measures plain average-error reduction; the 'safety' trade-off its title advertises is never tested.

The simulator's params.csv 'val' split (rows 600-899) holds exactly the public test's optics rows (kimi-k3__zzQfEQx [11]-[12]). Training on 'the supplied simulator' with all 900 rows (Kimi zzQfEQx, Grok vkezTdK, Gemini Flash GqqP35X) is allowed by the rule but makes the public sweep an in-distribution check. The private test uses 'new lens, distance and air settings', and the private/public reward ratios show no advantage for these trials.
verifier_issues: Public shards hold 20 clips, but private shards hold up to 48 within the same 120 s limit (SHARD_CLIPS=48). Agents had to extrapolate runtime themselves: GPT 6RCWGpu measured 102.41 s per 48 clips and GPT wf7cQhW 108 s for one candidate. All passed, but a slower grading GPU could have zeroed the heavy-ensemble submissions.
The private breakdown reports only objective/baseline_objective, not the strong-bin PSNR delta, so gate compliance can be inferred only from valid=1.

Two trials (Gemini Flash GqqP35X, Grok EzQwRFv) have an official reward but rewards={} with ArtifactCollectionError. Their rewards (0.321, 0.360) match their public results scaled by the common private/public ratio (~1.2), so they look real but cannot be verified.
The private baseline_objective is constant (0.46737) across trials, and the private shuffle seed is secret per run; no drift was observed.
task_level.noise: Inference is deterministic on a fixed set of 420 clips, so the noise is negligible. Every trial's private reward is 1.13-1.25x its last public reward (Fable 0.642 -> 0.738, GPT wf7cQhW 0.554 -> 0.619, Kimi zzQfEQx 0.426 -> 0.484, Grok vkezTdK 0.287 -> 0.345, Gemini Flash Taw69S6 0.198 -> 0.237), and the public and private orderings agree. The model-level gaps that decide the Elo games (Fable 0.74/0.71 vs GPT 0.62/0.50 vs the rest at 0.24-0.48) are far larger than any plausible measurement noise. The only near-tie is Gemini Argon RaMGX2p 0.460 vs Kimi zzQfEQx 0.484.
task_level.epoch_rationale: The scoring is deterministic and the public and private orderings agree. The non-binding strong-bin gate and the 20-vs-48-clip timing mismatch are spec weaknesses but did not change any outcome; Fable wins clearly on both attempts.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: All gains are legitimate engineering on a strong pretrained model: MSE-aligned fine-tuning on the supplied simulator with strength-balanced or metric-weighted sampling, function-preserving depth/width growth (Net2Net-style), dihedral x time self-ensembles, weight soups, and (GPT) flow-guided temporal fusion. Small physics-motivated touches add little but are genuine: DC/mean matching (Fable eTezLSD) and output extrapolation to counter ensemble over-smoothing. There was no test-data training, no cross-call state and no severity-label leakage. The benchmark-adjacent behaviours (training on val-split optics rows, bin weights set from public per-bin results) are allowed or negligible.

trials.approach: Long fine-tune (~190k iterations) of a grown MambaTM ('MambaTMx': 8 Mamba blocks plus zero-initialised residual 3-D-conv temporal fusion of the encoder skips) on on-the-fly simulator data. Training uses log-uniform D/r0 over 1.5-10 and only the simulator's train optics rows; the loss goes Charbonnier -> MSE with per-sample weights (D/r0/4)^-0.6 that mimic the per-bin relative-MSE metric, plus EMA. Inference runs a 16-pass dihedral x time-reversal self-ensemble with an adaptive wall-clock budget, plus 'DC matching' (shift each restored clip to the degraded input's mean, since turbulence preserves mean intensity).
